description: The real order path has no try/except around `client.create_and_post_order(...)` (order.py:72). If the CLOB API call throws (network error, signature rejection, HTTP error after the order was actually accepted server-side, response-parsing exception, etc.), the script crashes uncaught BEFORE reaching the ledger write at order.py:74-79. This means: (1) no local record is ever created for an order that may have actually posted server-side, (2) there is no reconciliation/retry-detection mechanism, so a subsequent cron tick has no way to know a real order for this token/window may already be in flight or filled, compounding the duplicate-order risk in FIND-001. A money-moving code path with zero failure handling is not verification-ready.

evidence.snippet:
resp = client.create_and_post_order(OrderArgs(token_id=token_id, price=price, size=shares, side=BUY))
oid = (resp or {}).get("orderID") or (resp or {}).get("id")
# ^ no try/except around create_and_post_order; ledger write only happens after this line succeeds
